Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 29:

﴿O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly⁠—﴾ by that which the Sharia has not permitted, such as usurpation (al-ghasb), usury (al-riba) and gambling (al-qimar). ﴿Except that it be a transaction conducted by mutual consent among you﴾. This is an exceptive of a disconnected kind (istithna' munqati'), meaning: but the occurrence of a transaction by mutual consent is not forbidden; or, intend the occurrence of a transaction. "By mutual consent" is a qualifier of "transaction," meaning a transaction issuing from the mutual consent of the contracting parties. The specification of trade (tijara) is because it is among the ways by which the property of another may lawfully be taken, since it is the most common and the most gentle for people of honour (dhawi al-muruwwat). It is also permissible that it be intended to mean transfer (al-intiqal) in general.

It has been said: the intended meaning of the prohibition is the restraint from spending wealth on what God does not approve, and by "trade" is meant spending it on what He approves. The Kufans read tijaratan with the accusative, on the basis of kana as a defective verb (kana al-naqisa) with an implied subject, meaning: except that the transaction or the matter be a transaction. ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾: by self-starvation (al-bakh'), as the ignorant of India do, or by casting oneself into destruction. This is supported by what is related: "that 'Amr ibn al-'As interpreted it as permitting tayammum due to fear of cold, and the Prophet ﷺ did not disapprove of it." Or it means committing that which leads to their killing, or perpetrating that which humiliates and destroys them, for that is the true killing of the self. It has also been said that the intended meaning of "selves" is those who are of their own religion, since the believers are like a single soul. In this injunction he combined the preservation of the self and of wealth, which is its sibling in that it is the cause of its sustenance, so that they may be given respite until souls complete themselves and attain their virtues, out of compassion and mercy toward them, as He indicated with His words: ﴿Indeed, God is ever merciful to you﴾, meaning: He commanded what He commanded and forbade what He forbade out of the abundance of His mercy upon you. It has also been said: its meaning is that He was merciful to you, O community of Muhammad, in that He commanded the Children of Israel to kill their own selves and forbade you from it.

﴿And whoever does that﴾ refers to the killing, or to the prohibited acts mentioned before it. ﴿In transgression and injustice﴾ means going to excess in exceeding the truth and doing what he does not deserve. It was said that he meant by transgression ('udwan) aggression against others, and by injustice (zulm) wronging oneself by exposing it to punishment. ﴿Then We will drive him into Fire﴾ means We will make him enter it. It was also read with the doubling of the lam, from ṣalla, and with a fatha on the nun, from ṣallāhu, yuṣalliyhi. From this comes the phrase shāh muṣalliyah (a sheep roasted over the fire). It was read as yuṣalliyhi with the ya', and the pronoun refers either to Allah, the Exalted, or to that act, inasmuch as it is the cause of being burned. ﴿And that is for Allah easy﴾ means there is no difficulty in it, and nothing turns Him away from it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 31:

﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden⁠—﴾ the major sins (kaba'ir al-dhunub) which Allah and His Messenger have forbidden you. It is also read as "kabira" (kabira), with the intention of the category (al-jins). ﴿We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾: We will forgive your minor sins (saghair) and erase them from you.

There is disagreement concerning the major sins (kaba'ir). The more correct view is that a major sin (kabira) is every sin for which the Lawgiver has prescribed a legal penalty (hadd) or explicitly threatened punishment. It has also been said: what is known to be forbidden by a definitive proof (qati').

It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that they are seven: associating partners with Allah, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden, slandering chaste women (qadhf al-muhsanat), consuming the property of orphans, usury (riba), fleeing from the battlefield, and disobedience to one's parents (uquq al-walidayn). And from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both:

(The major sins are closer to seven hundred than to seven.) It has also been said that he meant here the kinds of polytheism, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾. It has also been said that the smallness and greatness of sins is relative to what is above and below them: the greatest of the major sins is shirk, and the least of the minor sins is inner discourse of the self (hadith al-nafs). Between them are intermediate levels to which both descriptions apply. Whoever is faced with two of these and his soul is drawn to both in such a way that he cannot restrain himself, but he refrains from the greater of the two, Allah will expiate what he committed, in return for the reward he deserves for avoiding the greater.

Perhaps this varies according to persons and circumstances. Do you not see that He rebuked His Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, for many of his passing thoughts which would not be counted as a sin for others, let alone that He would hold him accountable for them? ﴿And We will admit you to a noble entrance﴾: Paradise and the reward He has promised, or entrance accompanied by honor. Nafi' read it here and in al-Hajj with a fatha on the mim (mudkhalan), and it may also be understood as a place or as a verbal noun.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 32:

﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others.﴾ Among worldly matters, such as status and wealth. For perhaps its absence is better, and what calls for the prohibition is that it leads to envy and mutual enmity, and expresses dissatisfaction with what Allah has apportioned to him, and is a craving for obtaining the thing without seeking it, which is blameworthy. For wishing for what has not been decreed for one is opposition to the wisdom of the decree; wishing for what has been decreed for one without earning it is idleness and the squandering of one's portion; and wishing for what has been decreed for one without any effort is futile and impossible. ﴿For men there is a share of what they have earned, and for women there is a share of what they have earned.﴾ This is an explanation of that: that is, for each of the men and the women there is a bounty and a share by reason of what they have earned and on account of it. So seek Allah's bounty through action, not through envy. As the Prophet (ﷺ), upon him be peace, said: "Faith is not by wishful thinking."

It has been said that the intended meaning is the share of inheritance, and the preference of heirs over one another in it, and that what is apportioned to each of them is according to what He knows of his condition, which necessitates increase and decrease, like one who earns it. ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty.﴾ That is, do not wish for what belongs to people; rather, ask Allah for the like of it from His treasuries, which never run out. This indicates that what is forbidden is envy. Or [the meaning is]: do not wish, and ask Allah of His bounty by that which brings it near and drives it to you. Ibn Kathir and al-Kisa'i read "wasalu Allaha min fadlihi" and "sal-hum fa-sal" and similar forms when it is an imperative addressed directly, with a waw or fa' before the sin without a hamza; and Hamzah, when pausing, follows his usual practice; and the rest read with the hamza. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ So He knows what each person deserves, and He bestows bounty with knowledge and clarification.

It is narrated that Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, men go out to fight and we do not fight, and we only have half the inheritance. I wish we were men." So this was revealed.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 33:

﴿And for each We have appointed heirs (mawali) to what the parents and the close relatives leave behind﴾. That is: for every estate We have appointed heirs who take charge of it and safeguard it. The phrase "to what the parents and the close relatives leave behind" is an explanation (bayan) of "each", with the separation by the governing element. Or: for every deceased person We have appointed heirs to what he left, with "from what" being attached to "mawali", because it carries the meaning of "heir". The omission of the pronoun of "each" and the words "the parents and the close relatives" constitutes a resumptive clause (isti'naf) explaining "mawali", and in it is the exclusion of children, for the close relatives do not include them, just as they do not include the parents. Or: for every people We have made mawali, a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave behind, with "We have made mawali" being a qualifier (sifa) of "each", and its returning pronoun being omitted in this case; so the sentence is composed of a subject and a predicate.

﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you﴾: these are the mawali of alliance (muwalah). The ally used to inherit a sixth (sudus) of his ally's property, and this was abrogated by His words: ﴿And those who are related by blood are closer to one another﴾. It is related from Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him: if a man embraced Islam at the hand of another man and they contracted to be each other's aqilah (bearers of blood-money) and to inherit from each other, the contract is valid and he inherits. Or: the words refer to spouses, the contract being the marriage contract, and "those" is a subject (mubtada') that carries the meaning of a condition, with its predicate.

﴿So give them their share﴾. Or it is in the accusative, governed by a hidden verb explained by what follows it, as in your saying: "Zayd, so strike him." Or it is conjoined to "the parents", and His words "so give them" are a clause caused by the preceding clause, emphasizing it, with the pronoun referring to the mawali.

The Kufans read "'aqqadat" (with the doubled 'qaf'), meaning: "their covenants were made by your oaths", so the word "covenants" (al-'uhud) was omitted, the pronoun attached to it was put in its place, and then it was omitted as it was omitted in the other reading.

﴿Indeed Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾: this is a warning against withholding their share.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 34:

﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women﴾ They stand over them in the manner of rulers over their subjects. He gives the reason for this with two matters, one innate and one acquired, saying: ﴿because Allah has made some of them to excel over others﴾, by reason of His exalting men over women with perfection of intellect, good management, and greater strength in deeds and acts of obedience. For this reason they were singled out for prophethood, the imamate, guardianship, the establishment of the rites, testimony in the principal matters of judgment, the obligation of jihad and the Friday prayer and the like, agnatic inheritance, the increased share in inheritance, and the exclusive right to divorce. ﴿And because they spend of their wealth﴾ on their wives, such as the bridal gift (mahr) and maintenance (nafaqah).

It has been narrated that Sa'd ibn al-Rabi', one of the chiefs (nuqaba') of the Ansar, was disobeyed by his wife Habibah bint Zayd ibn Abi Zuhayr, so he struck her, and her father went with her to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and complained. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let her take retaliation from him." Then the verse was revealed, and he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "We desired one thing and Allah desired another, and what Allah desired is better."

﴿So righteous women are devoutly obedient﴾, obedient to Allah, maintaining the rights of their husbands. ﴿Guarding in the husband's absence﴾ what is due to be guarded, meaning they guard in their husbands' absence what must be guarded regarding themselves and wealth. It is also narrated from him, peace be upon him: "The best of women is one who, when you look at her, pleases you; when you command her, she obeys you; and when you are absent from her, she guards you in her wealth and her person." Then he recited the verse.

It was also said: ﴿guarding what Allah has guarded﴾ means their secrets. ﴿With what Allah has guarded﴾ means by Allah's guarding of them through the command to guard the unseen, encouraging it by promise and warning, and granting them success in it; or by what Allah has guarded for them against men, such as the bridal gift, maintenance, the husband's care for them, and his defense of them. It has been read as "bima hafiza Allaha" in the accusative, taking "ma" as a relative pronoun; for if it were a verbal noun (masdariyyah), "hafiza" would have no subject, and the meaning would be: by the matter through which Allah's right and obedience are guarded, namely chastity and affection toward the men. ﴿And those from whom you fear disobedience﴾, that is, their disobedience and their haughtiness in refusing to comply with their husbands, from nushuz (rebellion). ﴿Admonish them, and forsake them in the beds﴾, meaning in the sleeping places, so do not let them under the covers; or do not be intimate with them, which is a metaphor for intercourse. It was also said that "al-madajic" means the places of spending the night, that is, do not spend the night with them. ﴿And strike them﴾, meaning a blow that is not severe and not disfiguring. These three matters are ordered, and one should proceed through them in sequence. ﴿Then if they obey you, do not seek a way against them﴾ by rebuke or harm. The meaning is: remove from them any molestation and treat what was from them as if it had not been, for the one who repents of a sin is like one who has no sin. ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Most High, Most Great﴾, so beware of Him, for He is more capable over you than you are over those under your hands; or, He is exalted in His dignity, pardons your misdeeds and turns to you in forgiveness, so you are more worthy of pardoning your wives; or, He is exalted and too great to wrong anyone or diminish his right.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 35:

﴿And if you fear a breach between the two﴾: a dispute between the wife and her husband. He (God) left them both implicit, although neither has been mentioned, because what indicates them has occurred. The attribution of the breach (shiqaq) to the adverbial phrase "between them" is either because it is treated as if it were the direct object, as in his saying: "O thief of the night, the people of the house," or because it is treated as the subject, as in their saying: "Your day is fasting."

﴿Then send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family﴾: O rulers, whenever their situation becomes unclear to you, send a man of moderation who is fit for judgment and reconciliation, from his family, and another from her family, so that the matter may be clarified or the relationship between them repaired. The relatives are more knowledgeable of the inner states of affairs and more eager for reconciliation. This is recommended (istihbab), and if they were appointed from outsiders, it would be permissible.

It has also been said that the address is to the husbands and wives, and this has been cited as evidence for the permissibility of arbitration. The more apparent view is that the appointment is for the purpose of reconciliation or clarification of the matter, and the two arbiters may not unite or separate the spouses except with the permission of the couple. Malik said: the two of them may arrange a khul' (separation by the wife's compensation) if they find it to be beneficial.

﴿If they both intend reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them﴾: The first pronoun refers to the two arbiters and the second to the spouses; that is, if the arbiters intend reconciliation, God will, through the goodness of their effort, bring about agreement between the spouses. It has also been said that both pronouns refer to the arbiters, meaning: if they intend reconciliation, God will bring harmony between them, so that their word becomes united and their aim is achieved. It has further been said that the pronouns refer to the spouses, meaning: if they both wish reconciliation and the removal of the breach, God will place affection and accord between them. In this there is an admonition that whoever sets his intention right in what he seeks, God will make right his objective.

﴿Indeed, God is ever Knowing, Acquainted﴾ with the apparent and the hidden, so He knows how to remove the breach and bring about accord.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 36:

﴿And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him﴾, [i.e., no idol or anything else], or any form of association (shirk), whether open (jali) or hidden (khafi). ﴿And to parents, good treatment﴾, and treat both of them well. ﴿And to near relatives﴾, and to the companion of kinship.

﴿And orphans, the needy, the neighbour who is near (dhi al-qurba)﴾ (p-74): that is, the one whose neighbourhood is near. It was also said that the neighbour who has a right of neighbourhood is one who is close and connected by a cause or by religion. It was also read in the accusative (al-nasb) on the basis of specification (al-ikhtisas), to magnify his right. ﴿And the neighbour who is a stranger (al-junub)﴾, the distant one, or the one who has no kinship.

It is related from him, upon him be prayer and peace (ʿalayhi al-salat wa al-salam): "Neighbours are of three kinds." A neighbour who has three rights: the right of neighbourhood, the right of kinship, and the right of Islam. A neighbour who has two rights: the right of neighbourhood and the right of Islam. And a neighbour who has one right: the right of neighbourhood, and he is the polytheist from among the People of the Book.

﴿And the companion at your side﴾: the companion in a good matter, such as learning, business, a trade, or travel, since he has accompanied you (sahibaka) and has come to be at your side (janbika). It was also said that it is the wife. ﴿And the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil)﴾: the traveller, or the weak one. ﴿And what your right hands possess﴾: the slaves, male and female. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-conceited﴾: arrogant, who disdains his relatives, neighbours and companions and does not turn to them. ﴿Boastful﴾: who vaunts himself over them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 37:

﴿Those who are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon the people﴾ is a substitution (badal) for His words ﴿whoever is arrogant and boastful﴾ (4:36), or it is in the accusative on the basis of dispraise (dhamm), or in the nominative on the basis of dispraise, meaning: they are the ones who… Or it is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate (khabar) is omitted, its estimated form being: ﴿those who are niggardly with what they have been granted, and enjoin upon the people niggardliness with it.﴾ Hamza and al-Kisa'i read bil-bukhl (بِالبُخْلِ) here and in "al-Hadid" with both letters vocalized with a fatha, and this is a dialectal form (lughah).

﴿And conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾: wealth and knowledge. Thus they deserve every censure.

﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾: the apparent noun was placed in the position of the pronoun, to indicate that whoever has this trait is a disbeliever in the blessing of Allah, and whoever is a disbeliever in the blessing of Allah, for him is a punishment that humiliates him, just as he humiliated the blessing through niggardliness and concealment.

The verse was revealed concerning a group of Jews who used to say to the Ansar, out of sincere advice: "Do not spend your wealth, for we fear poverty for you." It was also said that it was about those who concealed the description of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 38:

﴿And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people﴾ is conjoined with "those who are stingy," or with "the disbelievers." He associated them with the blame and the threat because stinginess and extravagance, which is spending not on those who deserve it, are two extremes of excess and deficiency, equal in ugliness and in drawing censure. Or it is a new subject (mubtada') whose predicate (khabar) is omitted, indicated by His saying: ﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion﴾.

﴿And they do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day﴾: so that by their spending they would seek His pleasure and His reward. They were the polytheists of Makkah. It was also said they were the hypocrites (munafiqun).

﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion, then evil is the companion he has﴾: an alert that Satan has joined them and driven them to this and adorned it for them, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the squanderers are brothers of the devils﴾. The intended meaning is Iblis and his helpers, both those within and those without. It is also permissible that this be a threat to them, that Satan be joined with them in the Fire.

That is, what is it that would be upon them, or what consequence would befall them because of faith and spending in the way of God? This is a rebuke (tawbikh) to them for their ignorance of where the benefit lies and for holding a belief about a thing contrary to what it is. It is also an incitement to reflection in seeking the answer, which may lead them to knowledge of the sublime benefits and beautiful outcomes it contains. And it is an alert that one who is invited to something harmless should respond to it out of caution, so how much more when it includes benefits. He placed faith first here and delayed it in the other verse because the purpose of mentioning it here is specification and causation. Then ﴿And God is ever Knowing of them﴾ is a warning to them. (p-75)

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 40:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom﴾ He does not diminish the reward, nor increase the punishment, by the smallest thing, like the dharra (atom), which is a tiny ant. It is also said of every part of the dust particles (haba'). The mithqal (weight) is a mif'al from the thiql (heaviness). Mentioning it hints that, although its measure is small, its recompense is great. ﴿And if it is a good deed﴾ and if the weight of the atom is a good deed. He made the pronoun feminine because the predicate is feminine, or because the mithqal is attributed to a feminine noun. He dropped the nun without analogical basis, likening it to the weak letters (huruf al-'illa). Ibn Kathir and Nafi' read ḥasanatun with a nominative ending, on the basis of kana being the complete (tamma) verb. ﴿He multiplies it﴾ He multiplies its reward. Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub read yud'if, and both have the same meaning.

﴿And gives from Himself﴾ He gives its doer from His own presence, by way of grace, beyond what He promised in return for the deed, ﴿a great reward﴾, a generous bestowal. He called it ajr (reward) though it is an addition to the reward, because it follows the reward and exceeds it.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on Surah 4, verses 41–42:**

﴿Then how?﴾ That is, how will be the condition of these disbelievers, from among the Jews, the Christians and others? ﴿When We bring from every nation a witness﴾, meaning their prophet, who will testify to the corruption of their beliefs and the ugliness of their deeds. The element governing the adverb of time (*zarf*) is the meaning of the subject and predicate (*mubtada'* and *khabar*), namely the terror of the matter and the magnification of its significance. ﴿And We bring you, O Muhammad, as a witness against these.﴾ You will bear witness to the truthfulness of these witnesses, because of your knowledge of their beliefs and your comprehension of the full scope of their rules, by means of your Law (*shar'*). It has been said that "these" refers to the disbelievers whose condition was asked about. It has also been said that it refers to the believers, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That you may be witnesses over mankind, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾.

﴿On that day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them﴾ This explains their state at that time. That is, those who combined disbelief with disobedience of the command, or the disbelievers and the sinners at that time, will wish that they were buried so that the earth would be leveled over them like the dead. Or they will wish they had not been resurrected or had not been created, and that they and the earth were equal. ﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾, meaning they will be unable to conceal it, because their own limbs will bear witness against them. It has also been said that the *waw* is for the circumstantial clause (*hal*), meaning: they wish that the earth were leveled over them, while their state is that they conceal nothing from Allah, and they do not deny Him by saying ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾. It was narrated that when they said this, Allah would set a seal upon their mouths, so their limbs would bear witness against them, the matter would grow severe for them, and they would wish that the earth were leveled over them.

Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read *tusawwā bihim* (تُسَوّى بِهِمْ), on the basis that the original form was *tatasawwā* (تَتَسَوّى), and the *tā'* was assimilated into the *sīn*. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *tusawwā* (تُسَوّى) by deleting the second *tā'*. It is said: *sawwaytuhu*, so *fa-tasawwā*.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 43:

﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying﴾ — meaning: do not stand to it while you are intoxicated from something like sleep or wine, until you have come to your senses and know what you are saying in your prayer.

It is narrated that ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf (may Allah be pleased with him) prepared a banquet and invited a group of the Companions, at a time when wine was still permissible. They ate and drank until they became intoxicated, and the time of the Maghrib prayer came, and one of them went forward to lead them in prayer and recited: "I worship what you worship." So this was revealed.

It has also been said that by "prayer" is meant its places, namely the mosques, and that the intended meaning is not a prohibition on the intoxicated approaching prayer; rather, the intended meaning is a prohibition on excess in drinking. "Sukr" (intoxication) derives from "sukr" (blocking), meaning obstruction. It has been read as "sakara" with a fatha and "sakra," as a plural like "halki" (the destroyed). Or it is a singular with the meaning "while you are a sukra people," or a group "sukra," and "sukra" like "hubla," as an adjective of the group. ﴿Nor in a state of major impurity (junub)﴾ is coordinated with His saying "while you are intoxicated," since the clause is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl). A junub is one who has been affected by janabah (major ritual impurity), and the term applies equally to the masculine and feminine, the singular and plural, since it is treated as a verbal noun (maṣdar). ﴿Except as travelers in transit﴾ is connected to His saying "nor in a state of major impurity," being an exception from the most general of states; that is, do not approach prayer in major impurity in most circumstances, except while traveling, and that is when one does not find water and performs tayammum (dry ablution). The mention of tayammum that follows supports this. Or it is an adjective of "junub," meaning: junub, not travelers in transit. In this is evidence that tayammum does not lift the minor ritual impurity (ḥadath). Whoever interprets "prayer" as its places interprets "travelers in transit" as those passing through them, and permits the junub to cross the mosque. This is the view of al-Shafiʿi (may Allah be pleased with him). Abu Hanifa (may Allah be pleased with him) said: it is not permissible for him to pass through the mosque unless there is water in it or it is a thoroughfare.

﴿Until you wash yourselves﴾ is the limit of the prohibition on approaching while in major impurity. The verse contains a reminder that the one who prays should guard against whatever distracts him and occupies his heart, and should purify himself of what must be purified from.

﴿And if you are ill﴾ — an illness in which one fears harm from using water, for one who has water is like one who lacks it. Or an illness that prevents him from reaching it. ﴿Or on a journey﴾ in which you do not find it. ﴿Or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself﴾ and has become impure by the emergence of something from one of the two passages. The origin of "ghait" is a low, depressed place of the ground. ﴿Or you have touched women﴾ — or you have touched their skin with your skin. Al-Shafiʿi derived from this that touching nullifies ablution. It has also been said: "or you have had intercourse with them." Ḥamza and al-Kisa'i read here and in al-Ma'ida "lamastum" (you have touched); using it as a metaphor for intercourse is less common than "mulamasa" (touching). ﴿And you find no water﴾ — you are not able to use it, since one who is prevented from it is like one who has lost it. The reasoning behind this division is that one who is permitted tayammum is either minor-impure (muḥdith) or major-impure (junub), and the situation that calls for it in most cases is illness or travel. Since the junub was mentioned earlier, its condition was described alone, while for the minor-impure, what was not previously mentioned, the causes were mentioned, both those that arise directly and those that arise incidentally; and the details of his condition were dispensed with by detailing the condition of the junub and stating the excuse in general terms. It is as if it were said: "And if you are junub, ill, or on a journey, or minor-impure, having come from the place of relieving oneself, or having touched women, and you find no water, ﴿then go to clean, good earth and wipe your faces and hands﴾" — that is, intend some clean part of the surface of the earth. For this reason the Hanafis said: if the one performing tayammum strikes his hand on a hard rock and wipes with it, it suffices. Our companions (the Shafiʿis) said: some dust must cling to the hand, due to His saying in al-Ma'ida, ﴿wipe your faces and hands with it﴾, that is, with some of it; and making "min" (with/from) denote the starting point is strained, since nothing from such a phrase is understood except partiality. The hand is the name of the limb up to the shoulder. What is narrated, that he (peace be upon him) performed tayammum and wiped his hands up to his elbows, and analogy with ablution, is evidence that what is meant here is "and your hands" up to the elbows. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾ — therefore He has made the matter easy for you and granted you concession.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 44–45:

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book?﴾ The seeing here may be sight (ru'yat al-basar), meaning, "Have you not looked at them?", or it may be seeing of the heart (al-qalb). It is transitive with "ila" (to) so that it includes the meaning of reaching (al-intiha').

﴿A portion of the Book﴾: a small share of knowledge of the Torah, because what is meant are the rabbis (ahbar) of the Jews.

﴿They buy error﴾: they choose it over guidance, or they exchange it for guidance after having attained it, or after it has come to them, by denying the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said: they take bribes (al-rushā) and distort the Torah.

﴿And they wish that you would go astray﴾, O believers, ﴿from the way﴾, the way of truth.

﴿And Allah is most knowing﴾ of you ﴿about your enemies﴾, and He has informed you of the enmity of these people and what they intend for you, so beware of them. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Protector﴾, the one who takes charge of your affairs. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Helper﴾, who aids you, so rely upon Him and be content with Him over others. The particle "bi" (in) is added to the agent of "kafa" (suffice) to emphasize the connection of the predication (al-ittisal al-isnadi) with the connection of the genitive (al-ittisal al-idafi).

(p-77) "Among those who are Jews, they distort" (﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا يُحَرِّفُونَ﴾) is an explanatory clause for "those who were given a portion" (alladhina utu nasiba), for it may include them and others. What lies between them is a parenthetical interjection (i'tiraḍ), or an explanation of "your enemies" (a'da'ikum), or a complement (ṣila) to "a helper" (naṣīran). That is, He helps you against those who are Jews and protects you from them. Alternatively, it is the predicate of an omitted subject, whose description is "they distort."

"They distort the words from their places" (﴿الكَلِمَ عَنْ مَواضِعِهِ﴾): that is, among those who are Jews there are a people who distort the words (yuharrifuna al-kalima), i.e., they turn them away (yumīlūnahu) from their places where God placed them, by removing them from there and placing other things in them. Or they interpret them according to what they desire, thereby turning them away from what God revealed in them. It is also read "al-kilm" with a kasra on the kaf and a sukun on the lam, plural of "kalima," as a lightening of "kalima" (a word).

"And they say, 'We have heard'" (﴿وَيَقُولُونَ سَمِعْنا﴾): your saying. "'And we have disobeyed'" (﴿وَعَصَيْنا﴾): your command. "'And hear, without being heard'" (﴿واسْمَعْ غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍ﴾): that is, one who is cursed by you without you being heard, because of deafness or death; or, "hear, without being answered in what you call to"; or, "hear, without hearing from you anything you approve of"; or, "hear a word that is not made to be heard by you, because your ear recoils from it," in which case "unheard" is the object; or, "hear what is unpleasant, from their saying 'Aslama-hu fulan' (so-and-so cursed him) when he reviles him." They said this out of hypocrisy. "'And ra'ina'" (﴿وَراعِنا﴾): look at us, that we may speak to you, or that we may understand your speech.

"Twisting their tongues" (﴿لَيًّا بِألْسِنَتِهِمْ﴾): turning them with their tongues and diverting speech toward what resembles abuse, since they put "ra'ina," which resembles what they revile one another with, in place of "unzurna" (look at us), and "ghayra musmaʿin" in place of "la usmʿta makrūhan" (may you never be made to hear something disliked). Or it is twisting with their tongues and mixing what they manifest of supplication and reverence with what they conceal of abuse and contempt, out of hypocrisy. "And slandering the religion" (﴿وَطَعْنًا في الدِّينِ﴾): mocking it and ridiculing it.

"And if they had said, 'We have heard and obeyed, and hear, and look at us'" (﴿وَلَوْ أنَّهم قالُوا سَمِعْنا وأطَعْنا واسْمَعْ وانْظُرْنا﴾): and if their saying this had been established in place of what they said. "It would have been better for them and more upright" (﴿لَكانَ خَيْرًا لَهم وأقْوَمَ﴾): their saying that would have been better for them and more just. The verb after "law" must be omitted in such a case, because "anna" indicates it and it occupies its place. "But God cursed them for their disbelief" (﴿وَلَكِنْ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾): but God forsook them and removed them far from guidance because of their disbelief. "So they do not believe, except a few" (﴿فَلا يُؤْمِنُونَ إلا قَلِيلا﴾): that is, except a faith of little value, which is faith in some of the verses and messengers. It is possible that "few" is meant as "none," as in his saying: "Little complaint to the troubled one who is afflicted," or "except a few of them who believed or will believe."

﴿O you who were given the Book, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what you already have, before We obliterate faces and turn them back upon their backs﴾ before We efface the outline of their forms and make them into the likeness of their backs, meaning the napes of their necks, or We turn them backward in this world or in the Hereafter. The root meaning of *tams* (obliteration) is the removal of distinguishing marks, and it may also be used in the sense of *tals* (erasing a picture), and in the general sense of turning something over and changing it. For this reason it has been said that its meaning is: before We change faces, stripping them of their honor and favor, and clothing them in humiliation and retreat, or We turn them back to the place from which they came, which is Adhri'at in Syria, meaning the expulsion of the Banu al-Nadir. Close to this is the view of one who said that the intended meaning of "faces" is the leaders. Or it means: before We obliterate faces by blinding their sight from taking heed and deafening their hearing from listening to the truth through a natural seal, and turn them away from guidance to misguidance. ﴿Or curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath﴾, or humiliate them by transformation as We humiliated the people of the Sabbath with it, or transform them into a transformation like theirs, or curse them through your tongue as We cursed them through the tongue of Dawud (David). The pronoun refers either to the owners of the faces, or to those who are meant, by way of *iltifat* (a shift in grammatical person), or to "faces" if by it is meant the notables. Its being coordinated with *tamsi* (obliteration) in the first sense indicates that the intended meaning is not the transformation of the form in this world. Whoever understood the threat as a change of form in this world said that it is still awaited, or that its occurrence was conditional upon their not believing, and a group of them did believe. ﴿And the command of God was﴾ to bring about a thing or its threat, or what He decreed and ordained. ﴿Carried out﴾ executed and existing, so what you have been threatened with will certainly occur if you do not believe.(p-78)

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 48:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with partners﴾ because He has issued a definitive ruling concerning the eternity of its punishment, and because the stain of that sin does not get effaced from its perpetrator, so he is not prepared for pardon, unlike others. ﴿And He forgives what is less than that﴾ i.e., what is less than shirk, whether minor or major, ﴿for whomever He wills﴾ out of His bounty and kindness. The Mu'tazilah tied this to the two verbs, in the sense that Allah does not forgive shirk for whomever He wills, namely the one who does not repent, and forgives what is less than it for whomever He wills, namely the one who repents. But this is a restriction without evidence, since the generality of the verses of threat is no more deserving of being kept to than this; and it refutes their own doctrine, for making the matter contingent upon the will (mashi'ah) contradicts the obligation of punishment before repentance and pardon after it. So the verse, just as it is a proof against them, is also a proof against the Khawarij who claimed that every sin is shirk and that its doer is eternal in the Fire. ﴿And whoever associates partners with Allah has indeed fabricated a tremendous sin﴾: he committed what makes all other sins seem trivial by comparison. This points to the distinguishing meaning between it and all other sins. Al-iftira' (fabrication), just as it is applied to speech, is also applied to action, and likewise al-ikhtilaq.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 49–50:

﴿Have you not seen those who attribute purity to themselves?﴾ That is, the People of the Book, who said: "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved." It was also said: "Some Jews brought their children to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'Is there any sin upon these?' He said: 'No.' They said: 'By Allah, we are only like them. We did not do any deed by day, and it was expiated for us by night; and we did not do any deed by night, and it was expiated for us by day.'" And within their category is whoever praises himself and extols himself.

﴿Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills﴾ This is a reminder that His purification of someone is what counts, not the purification of anyone else, for He is the One who knows what a person harbors of good and evil. He censured them and praised the servants of His He approves of among the believers. The root meaning of tazkiyah (purification, i.e., declaring someone pure) is the negation of what is deemed ugly, whether in deed or in speech. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ by being blamed or punished for their declaring themselves pure without right. ﴿a fatil﴾ (the least amount of injustice, the smallest of it), which is the thread in the cleft of a date pit, a thing proverbial for its insignificance.

﴿Look how they fabricate lies against Allah﴾ in their claim that they are the sons of Allah and pure in His sight. ﴿And sufficient is it﴾ this claim of theirs, or the fabrication, ﴿as a manifest sin﴾ whose being a sin among their sins is not hidden.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 51:

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They believe in jibt and taghut﴾ It was revealed concerning the Jews who used to say that the worship of idols is more pleasing to God than what Muhammad calls them to. It is also said that it was revealed concerning Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and a group of Jews who went out to Mecca to form an alliance with the Quraysh against the Messenger of God (ﷺ). They said: "You are the People of the Book, and you are closer to Muhammad than we are, so we do not feel safe from your deception. Prostrate to our gods so that we may be reassured by you." So they did. Al-jibt (idol, sorcery) is originally the name of an idol, and it came to be used for everything worshipped besides God. It is also said that its origin is al-jibs, which is that in which there is no good, and its sin was changed into a ta'. Al-taghut is applied to every falsehood, whether a worshipped thing or otherwise. ﴿And they say to those who disbelieve﴾ on their account and concerning them. ﴿"These"﴾ is a reference to them.

﴿"They are better guided than those who believe in the way"﴾ more upright in religion and more rightly guided in path.

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed. And whoever Allah curses, you will not find for him any helper.﴾ He (the cursed one) is protected from punishment by him through intercession or otherwise.

﴿Or do they have a share of the kingdom?﴾ *Am* (أم) is *munqati'a* (disjunctive, مُنْقَطِعَة). The meaning of the *hamza* (همزة, the interrogative particle) is a denial that they have any share of the kingdom, and a rejection of what the Jews claimed, that the kingdom would pass to them. ﴿Then they would not give people even a *naqir*﴾: that is, if they had a share of the kingdom, then they would not give anyone anything equal to a *naqir* (نَقِير), which is the small notch on the back of a date stone. This is an exaggeration in describing their stinginess: if they withhold even a *naqir* while being kings, then what would you think of them when they are poor, humiliated and needy? It is also possible that the meaning is a denial that they were given any share of the kingdom, by way of *kinaya* (كناية, allusion or metonymy), and that they do not give people anything. When *fa-idhan* (فإذًا) comes after *wa* or *fa* and is not coordinating a single noun, it may be either *ilgha'* (إلغاء, nullified, i.e. not governing) or *i'mal* (إعمال, operative, governing). For this reason it has been read as ﴿*fa-idhan la yu'tuna al-nasa*﴾ with the verb in the accusative (عَلى النَّصْبِ).

﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾ Rather, do they envy the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions, or the Arabs, or all of humankind? Whoever envies [others] for prophethood (nubuwwah) has, in effect, envied all of humankind for their perfection and their guidance. He rebuked them and denounced their envy, just as He condemned them for stinginess (bukhl), and these two are among the worst of vices, and there seems to be a mutual implication and attraction between them. ﴿for what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾ meaning prophethood, the Book, victory, and honour, and He made the awaited Prophet to be from among them. ﴿We had already given the family of Abraham﴾ who are the ancestors of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the sons of his paternal uncles. ﴿the Scripture and wisdom﴾ meaning prophethood. ﴿and We had given them a great kingdom﴾ so it is not far-fetched that Allah should give him the like of what He gave them.

It has also been said that its meaning is: so among the family of Abraham were those who believed in it, and among them were those who disbelieved, and that did not weaken his affair; likewise, the disbelief of these people does not weaken your affair. ﴿And sufficient for them is Hellfire as a blaze﴾ a fire kindled, by which they will be punished; that is, if they are not hastened to punishment, then what has been prepared for them of the blazing fire of Hell is sufficient for them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 56–57:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our signs – We will surely burn them in Fire.﴾ This serves as an elaboration and affirmation of that. ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins, that they may taste the punishment.﴾ This may be by restoring that same skin in another form, as in your saying: "I changed the ring into an earring" (baddaltu al-khatam qirṭan); or by removing from it the trace of burning so that its sensation of the punishment returns, as He said: ﴿that they may taste the punishment﴾, i.e., that its tasting may continue for them. It was also said that He creates for them another skin in its place. The punishment in reality falls upon the disobedient soul which perceives, not upon the instrument of its perception, so there is no objection. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Mighty﴾, nothing He wills is prevented from Him, ﴿Wise﴾, He punishes in accordance with His wisdom.

﴿As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will admit them to Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever.﴾ He mentioned the disbelievers and their threat before the believers and their promise because the discourse is about them, and mention of the believers is incidental. ﴿For them therein are purified spouses, and We will admit them to a shade, deep and dense.﴾ A lasting, thick shade that is not interrupted, and one that the sun does not erase, which is an indication of complete and enduring blessing. "Ẓalīl" is a descriptive adjective derived from "ẓill" (shade) for emphasis, like their saying: "shamsun shāmis" (a blazing sun), "laylun alyal" (a pitch-black night), and "yawmun ayyam" (a long day).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 58:

﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render the trusts to their owners﴾. This is an address that encompasses all those who are legally responsible (mukallafun) and all trusts (amanat), although it was revealed on the day of the Conquest (Fath) concerning Uthman ibn Talha ibn Abd al-Dar, when he locked the door of the Ka'ba and refused to hand over the key so that the Messenger of Allah could enter it. He said: "If I had known that he was the Messenger of Allah, I would not have prevented him." Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, twisted his hand and took the key from him and opened the door. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered and prayed two rak'as. When he came out, al-Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) asked him to give him the key and to combine for him the office of providing water (siqaya) and the office of keeping the key (sadana). Then the verse was revealed, and Allah commanded him to return the key to him. So he commanded Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) to return it to him and to apologise to him. This became a cause of his conversion to Islam, and revelation came down that the keeping of the key (sadana) would remain in his descendants forever. ﴿And when you judge between people, to judge with justice﴾. That is: and that you judge with fairness and equity when you decide between those whose command is binding upon you, or who accept your judgment. And because judgment is the function of rulers, it was said that the address is to them. ﴿Indeed, how excellent is what Allah instructs you with﴾. That is: an excellent thing with which He instructs you, or the excellent thing with which He instructs you. Here "ma" is either in the accusative as a qualifying noun (mawsufa), described by "with which He instructs you," or in the nominative as a relative pronoun (mawsula) connected to it. The object of praise is omitted, and it is what is commanded: rendering trusts and justice in judgments. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing﴾, of your statements, your judgments, and what you do concerning trusts.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 59:

﴿O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you.﴾ He means by them the commanders of the Muslims during the time of the Messenger (ﷺ) and after him, and it includes the caliphs, the judges, and the commanders of the military expeditions (sariyyah). He commanded the people to obey them after He had commanded them to be just, as an alert that the obligation of obeying them lasts only as long as they are upon the truth. It has been said: they are the scholars of the Sharia, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, those who draw conclusions from it would have known it among them.﴾ ﴿And if you dispute﴾ among yourselves, you and those in authority among you, ﴿concerning anything﴾ of the affairs of the religion, and this supports the first view, since it is not permissible for the lay person (muqallid) to dispute with the mujtahid over his ruling, unlike the subordinate, unless it is said that the address to those in authority is by way of iltifat (a shift in grammatical person). ﴿Then refer it﴾ i.e., return to it for judgment, ﴿to Allah﴾ i.e., to His Book, ﴿and the Messenger﴾ by asking about it during his lifetime, and by returning to his Sunnah after him. The Mu'tazilah (Mu'tazila) and those who reject qiyas (analogical reasoning) cited this verse and said: He, exalted is He, obligated the referral of disputed matters to the Book and the Sunnah, not to qiyas. It has been answered that referring the disputed matter to what is textually stated (al-mansus alayh) occurs only through analogy (tamthil) and building upon it, and that is qiyas. This is supported by the command to do so following the command to obey Allah and obey His Messenger, for it indicates that the rulings are of three kinds: those established by the Book, those established by the Sunnah, and those established by referral to the two by way of qiyas. ﴿If you believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾ for faith necessitates this. ﴿That﴾ i.e., the referral, ﴿is better﴾ for you, ﴿and better in outcome﴾ (ta'wil), meaning in consequence, or better in interpretation (ta'wil) than your own interpretation without referral.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on surah 4, verse 60:

﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet they desire to take their disputes for judgment to the Taghut (false judge/idol)?﴾

From Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him both: "(A hypocrite disputed with a Jew. The Jew invited him to the Prophet ﷺ, and the hypocrite invited him to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. Then they both took their dispute to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he ruled in favour of the Jew. But the hypocrite was not satisfied with his judgment and said, 'Let us take it to Umar.' The Jew said to Umar, 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has ruled for me, but he was not satisfied with his judgment, so he has brought the dispute to you.' Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the hypocrite, 'Is that so?' He said, 'Yes.' Umar said, 'Stay where you are until I come out to you.' He went in, took his sword, then came out and struck the hypocrite's neck with it until he was cold dead, and said, 'This is how I judge for the one who is not satisfied with the judgment of Allah and His Messenger.' Then this verse was revealed.)"

Jibril (Gabriel) said: "Umar has distinguished between truth and falsehood, so he was named al-Faruq (the Distinguisher)."

On this account, the Taghut is Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. In its wider meaning, it refers to anyone who judges by falsehood and favours others for its sake. It was so called because of the extremity of his transgression (tughyan), or because he resembles the Shaytan (Satan), or because taking one's dispute to him is taking it to the Shaytan, in that the Shaytan is the one who prompts it, as Allah says:

﴿And they had been commanded to reject it, while Satan desires to lead them far astray.﴾

It has also been recited as "an yakfuru bihā" (that they reject them), on the basis that Taghut is a plural noun, as in Allah's words: ﴿Their protectors are the Taghut; they bring them out [of the light into darkness].﴾

"Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger" — ﴿وَإذا قِيلَ لَهم تَعالَوْا إلى ما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ وإلى الرَّسُولِ﴾ — And it is recited as «taʿālū» with a ḍammah on the lām, on the basis that the lām of the verb was elided irregularly (iʿtibāṭan) and then the lām was given a ḍammah for the wāw of the pronoun.

"You see the hypocrites turning away from you with [complete] aversion" — ﴿رَأيْتَ المُنافِقِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنْكَ صُدُودًا﴾ — ṣudūdan is either a verbal noun (maṣdar) or a noun standing in place of the verbal noun (ism li-l-maṣdar) of ṣadd, which is the act of turning away. The difference between it and sadd (barrier) is that the former is not perceptible, whereas the latter is perceptible. And yaṣuddūna is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl).

"How, then, [will it be] when a calamity strikes them" — ﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾ يَكُونُ حالُهم. ﴿إذا أصابَتْهم مُصِيبَةٌ﴾ — such as the killing of the hypocrite by ʿUmar, or retribution from Allah the Exalted — "for what their hands have sent forward" — ﴿بِما قَدَّمَتْ أيْدِيهِمْ﴾ — namely, their seeking judgment from other than you and their not being content with your ruling. "Then they come to you" — ﴿ثُمَّ جاءُوكَ﴾ — when they are struck, to offer excuses; it is coordinated with "strikes them." It has also been said that it is coordinated with "they turn away," and what lies between them is a parenthetical insertion (iʿtirāḍ).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 63:

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾ of hypocrisy, so concealment and false oaths will not avail them against the punishment.

﴿So turn away from them﴾, i.e., from punishing them, for a benefit in sparing them, or from accepting their excuses. ﴿And admonish them﴾ with your tongue and restrain them from what they are upon. ﴿And say to them concerning themselves﴾, i.e., in the sense of "about themselves," or privately with them, for advice in secret is more effective. ﴿A far-reaching word﴾ that reaches them and has an effect upon them. He was commanded to overlook their sins, to advise them, and to exert effort in it through encouragement and warning, and this is what the compassion of the Prophets, upon them be peace, requires. Attaching the adverbial phrase to "far-reaching" with the meaning "far-reaching concerning themselves, having an effect upon them" is weak, because the complement of a modifier does not precede the modified noun. The far-reaching word, in its basic sense, is the one that corresponds to its intended meaning.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 64:

﴿And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by the permission of Allah﴾ — that is, by reason of His permission in obedience to him and His command to those to whom he was sent that they should obey him. It seems that he (al-Baydawi) argues from this that whoever is not content with his judgment, even if he manifests Islam, is an unbeliever deserving of death. Its statement is: since the sending of a messenger was only so that he would be obeyed, whoever does not obey him and is not content with his judgment has not accepted his message, and whoever is like that is an unbeliever deserving of death.

﴿And if, when they had wronged themselves﴾ — by hypocrisy or by seeking judgment from the taghut (false object of worship, transgressor).

﴿they had come to you﴾ — repenting of that. The predicate of inna is here, and idh is connected to it.

﴿and asked Allah's forgiveness﴾ — through repentance and sincerity.

﴿and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them﴾ — and apologised to you, until you stood up for them as an intercessor. The address was shifted to glorify his station and to alert that it is part of the right of the Messenger to accept the apology of the penitent, however great his sin, and to intercede for him, and it is part of his office to intercede for major sins.

﴿they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾ — they would have known Him to be accepting of their repentance and graciously bestowing mercy upon them. If "found" (wajada) is interpreted as "encountered" (sadafa), then "accepting of repentance" is a circumstantial state (hal), and "Merciful" is either a substitute for it or a circumstantial state from the pronoun within it.

(p-82) ﴿So, by your Lord﴾, i.e., "by your Lord"; the particle "lā" is extra, serving to emphasize the oath, not to negate. It is not [a negation] of the verb in His saying "lā ﴿yu'minūn﴾" (they do not believe), because it is also used as an extra particle in affirmative statements, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I swear by this city﴾ (lā uqsimu bihādhā al-balad). ﴿Until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves﴾, i.e., in what has become disputed and confused among them; and from this comes the word shajar (tree), because its branches intertwine. ﴿Then they find within themselves no discomfort (ḥaraj) regarding what you have decided﴾, i.e., no constriction regarding what you have judged, or [regarding] your judgment, or doubt concerning it, for the doubter is in constriction about his matter. ﴿And submit with full submission﴾, i.e., yield to you in full compliance, outwardly and inwardly.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 66:

﴿And if We had prescribed for them, "Kill yourselves," or "Leave your homes,"﴾ Dhalika is not the subject here. The verse reads: ﴿And if We had prescribed for them, "Kill yourselves"﴾, meaning expose yourselves to being killed in jihad, or "Kill them (yourselves) as the Children of Israel killed," and *an* (أنْ) is either a verbal particle (مَصْدَرِيَّةٌ, *masdariyyah*) or an explanatory particle (مُفَسِّرَةٌ, *mufassirah*), because *kataba* (كَتَبْنا, "We prescribed") here carries the meaning of *amarna* (أمَرْنا, "We commanded"). ﴿Or "Leave your homes"﴾: their leaving was when they were asked to repent of worshipping the calf. Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub read *an-quluu* (أنِ اقْتُلُوا) with a kasra on the nun, according to the original vowel of the sound, and *akhrujuu* (اخْرُجُوُا) with a damma on the waw, by assimilation and by analogy with the waw of the plural in such words as the verse: ﴿And do not forget bounty among yourselves﴾ (2:237). Hamza and 'Asim read both with a kasra, according to the original form, while the rest read both with a damma, treating them as they would treat a hamza joined to the verb. ﴿They would not have done it, except a few of them﴾: except a few people, and they are the sincere ones. When He made clear that their faith is not complete unless they submit fully, He drew attention to the deficiency of most of them and the weakness of their Islam. The pronoun refers to what was prescribed, which is indicated by *kataba*, or it refers to one of the two verbal nouns of the two verbs. Ibn 'Amir read *illa qalilan* with the accusative, as an exception (اسْتِثْناء, *istithna'*), or as "except a little action." ﴿And if they had done what they were admonished with﴾: following the Messenger (ﷺ), obeying him willingly and eagerly. ﴿It would have been better for them﴾ in their immediate and their ultimate affairs. ﴿And firmer in establishing [their faith]﴾ in their religion, because it is more conducive to acquiring knowledge and removing doubt, or it establishes the reward of their deeds. Its accusative is as a specification (تَمْيِيز, *tamyiz*). The verse was also revealed about the hypocrite and the Jew. It has been said that it and the verse before it were revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a, who disputed with al-Zubayr over the watercourses of al-Jarra, which they used to irrigate the palm trees. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, then send the water to your neighbour." Hatib said: "Even if he is the son of your paternal aunt?" Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, then hold back the water until it reaches the walls, take your full right, and then release it to your neighbour."

﴿And [if they had done so] We would have given them from Us a great reward.﴾ This answers an implied question, as if it were said: "What would they receive after being firm?" So He said: "And then [*idhan*, a particle of response and condition], if they had been firm, We would have given them..." because *idhan* is both an answer and a condition.

﴿And We would have guided them to a straight path.﴾ Through following it they reach the sacred presence (*janab al-quds*), and He opens to them the doors of the unseen (*al-ghayb*). The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever acts upon what he knows, Allah will bequeath to him the knowledge of what he did not know."

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 69–70:

﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – then those are with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour﴾ – an added encouragement to obedience, by promising, as its reward, companionship with the noblest of creation and the most exalted of them in rank. ﴿Of the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs, and the righteous﴾ – an explanation of "those" (alladhina), or a circumstantial clause (hal) from it, or from its pronoun. He divided them into four categories according to their ranks in knowledge and action, and urged all people not to fall behind them. They are: the prophets, who attained the perfection of knowledge and action and went beyond the limit of perfection to the level of bringing perfection to others. Then the truthful (al-siddiqun), whose souls ascended, at times by the ladders of reflection upon proofs and signs, and at other times by the paths of purification and spiritual discipline, to the summit of gnosis (irfan), until they perceived things and reported about them as they truly are. Then the martyrs, whose eagerness for obedience and their earnest striving (jidd) in manifesting the truth (p-83) led them to sacrifice their lives in exalting the Word of Allah, the Exalted. Then the righteous, who spent their lives in His obedience and their wealth in seeking His good pleasure. You may also say: those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour are the gnostics of Allah, and these [gnostics] are either those who have reached the degree of direct vision (ayn), or those who remain at the station of inference and demonstration. The first group either attain, together with direct vision, nearness such that they are like one who sees a thing close at hand – and these are the prophets, upon them be blessings and peace – or they do not, and then they are like one who sees a thing from afar – and these are the truthful. The second group either have their gnosis through decisive proofs – and these are the firmly rooted scholars in knowledge, who are the witnesses of Allah on His earth – or their gnosis is through indications and persuasions in which their souls find rest, and these are the righteous. ﴿And excellent are those as companions﴾ – this carries the sense of wonder (ta'ajjub). "Rafiqan" is in the accusative as a specification (tamyiz) or as a circumstantial state (hal). It is not made plural, because it is used for the singular and the plural alike, as in "siddiq"; or because it is intended as: each one of them is an excellent companion.

It is narrated that "Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), came to him one day, his face changed and his body emaciated. He asked him about his condition, and he said: 'Nothing ails me, except that whenever I do not see you, I long for you and feel a severe loneliness until I meet you. Then I remembered the Hereafter, and I feared that I would not see you there, because I know that you will be raised up with the prophets; and if I enter Paradise, I will be in a station below yours; and if I do not enter, then that is the time when I shall never see you ever.' Then this verse was revealed."

﴿That﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), a reference to what the obedient receive of reward, increased guidance, and companionship with those upon whom favour has been bestowed; or a reference to the excellence and distinction of those favoured ones. ﴿The bounty﴾ is its attribute. ﴿From Allah﴾ is its predicate; or "the bounty" is the predicate and "from Allah" is a circumstantial clause, its governing element being the sense of the demonstrative. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Knower﴾ – of the reward of whoever obeys Him, or of the measures of bounty and the worthiness of its recipients.

﴿O you who believe, take your precautions.﴾ Be alert and prepare yourselves against the enemies. *Al-hadhar* (الحَذَر) and *al-hadhr* (الحَذْر) are like *al-athar* (الأثَر) and *al-athr* (الأثْر), two vocalizations of the same noun. It is also said that *al-hadhar* refers to what one guards oneself with, such as armor and weapons.

﴿then go forth﴾ means go out to jihad. ﴿in groups﴾ (*thubat*, ثُباتٍ) means scattered bands. It is the plural of *thubah* (ثُبَة), from the expression *thabaytu 'ala fulan tathbiyatan* (ثَبَيْتُ عَلى فُلانٍ تَثْبِيَةً), meaning that one mentions the scattered good qualities of a person. It is also pluralized as *thabin* (ثَبِينٍ), a form used to compensate for what was dropped from the end of the word. ﴿or go forth all together﴾ means gathered as a single troop (*kawkabah*, كَوْكَبَةً). Although the verse was revealed concerning war, the unrestricted wording requires hastening to all good deeds in every way possible before they are lost.

﴿And among you is one who will surely lag behind.﴾ The address is to the army of the Messenger (ﷺ), both its believers and its hypocrites. Those who lag behind (*al-mubti'un*, المُبْطِئُون) are the hypocrites among them, who grew sluggish and stayed away from jihad. The verb *batta'a* (بَطَّأ) may be used in the sense of *ab'ata* (أبْطَأ), which is intransitive. Or it may mean that they discouraged others, as Ibn Ubayy discouraged people on the day of Uhud. *Batta'a* here is a transitive form derived from *ba'ufa* (بَطُؤَ), just as *thaqqala* (ثَقَّلَ) is derived from *thaqula* (ثَقُلَ).

Grammatically, the first *lam* (لام الابتداء, the emphatic *lam* of beginning) entered on the subject of *inna* (إنَّ) because the predicate intervened. The second *lam* is the answer to an omitted oath. The oath together with its answer forms the relative clause (*silah*, صِلَة) of *min* (مِن). The returning pronoun is the hidden pronoun within *leyubatti'anna* (لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ). The implied sense is: "And among you is one who swore by Allah that he would surely lag behind."

﴿If a calamity befalls you﴾ such as killing or defeat. ﴿He will say﴾ meaning the one who lags behind. ﴿Allah has blessed me, for I was not present with them as a witness﴾, meaning present, so that what befell them would befall me.

And if a bounty from God befalls you, such as a conquest or spoils of war, he will surely say, with the emphasis (ta'kīd) of the lām and nūn indicating the intensity of his regret: "(Ṭāʾifa) ...". ﴿as though there had never been any affection between you and him﴾ is an interjected clause (i'tirāḍ, a parenthetical phrase) placed between the verb and its object, which is the pronoun *hu* (هُ).

"Oh, I wish I had been with them."

It has been said that this clause is connected to the first sentence, but this is weak, since the parts of a sentence are not separated by something that is not connected to them either in wording or in meaning. *Ka-anna* is the light form (mukhaffafa, the lightened form of *inna*) of the heavy form, and its noun is the dummy pronoun (ḍamīr al-sha'n, the pronoun of the matter), which is omitted.
